DIRECTOR FELICIANO REGIS OPA, This Department Dear Director Regis: This has reference to the text from 09484936969 asking clarification on this issue: "DILG on legal opinion of june 2010 re punong barangay to seek permission from the department when practicing profession, I think department means the head of office and not dilg because you are quoting a civil service rule pls check tnx much". Said query was forwarded to this level by the Public Assistance and Complaint Center, this Department, thru an Information Sheet dated 02 December 2011. Perhaps, the texter is referring to DILG Opinion No. 29, series of 201 1 dated 27 June 201 1 and June 2010. Pertinent portion of DILG Opinion No. 29, series of 201 1 is quoted hereunder, thus: "Be that as it may, while punong barangay is allowed to practice his/her profession, however, being a public official, he/she must first obtain prior written permission from the head of the Department concerned as required under Section 12, Rule XVIII of the Revised Civil Service Rules which provides and we quote: 'Section 12. No officer or employee shall engage directly in any private business, vocation, or profession or be connected with any commercial credit agriculture or industrial undertaking without a written permission from the head of the department". Also, in the case of Wilfredo M. Catu vs. Atty. Vicente G. Rellosa (A.C. No. 5738, February 19, 2008) the Supreme Court ruled that a Punong Barangay should obtain prior written permission from the Secretary of the Department of the Interior and Local Government. Applying the Supreme Court ruling to your query, we are of the view that all Punong Barangays shall obtain first a prior written permission from the Secretary of the Department of the Interior and Local Government before they can practice their profession or engage in other occupation. "(Emphasis Supplied) The texter is of the view that the phrase "head of the department" underlined above pertaining to the authority from which Punong Barangays should obtain prior written permission before they can practice their profession or engage in other occupation, means the "head of the office" and not this Department as we interpreted in the assailed opinion. Hence, his/her suggestion for us to check the aforesaid opinion.

We maintain our opinion under DILG Opinion No. 29, series of 201 1 dated 27 June 2011. If said texter had only the chance to read the case of Wilfredo M. Catu vs. Atty. Vicente G. Rellosa (A.C. No. 5738, 19 February 2008), which we cited in the assailed opinion, he/she would know that it was not us who gave such interpretation but it was the Supreme Court itself. The Supreme Court categorically ruled therein and we quote: "A civil service officer or employee whose responsibilities do not require his time to be fully at the disposal of the government can engage in the private practice of law only with the written permission of the head of the department concerned. Section 12, Rule XVIII of the Revised Civil Service Rules provides: Sec. 12. No officer or employee shall enqaqe directly in any private business, vocation, or profession or be connected with any commercial, credit, agricultural, or industrial undertaking without a written permission from the head of the Department: Provided, That this prohibition will be absolute in the case of those officers and employees whose duties and responsibilities require that their entire time be at the disposal of the Government; Provided, further, That if an employee is granted permission to engage in outside activities, time so devoted outside of office hours should be fixed by the agency to the end that it will not impair in any way the efficiency of the officer or employee: And provided, finally, that no permission is necessary in the case of investments, made by an officer or employee, which do not involve real or apparent conflict between his private interests and public duties, or in any way influence him in the discharge of his duties, and he shall not take part in the management of the enterprise or become an officer of the board of directors. As punong barangay, respondent should have therefore obtained the prior written permission of the Secretary of Interior and Local Government before he entered his appearance as counsel for Elizabeth and Pastor. This he failed to do. (Emphasis Supplied) Article 8 of the Civil Code states that "Judicial decisions applying or interpreting the laws or the Constitution shall form part of the legal system of the Philippines". Said pronouncement of the Court in the case of Catu vs. Rellosa, having formed part of the law of the land, ignorance thereof can no longer be countenanced. Please be guided accordingly. Very truly yours, SUSB. Q IV Direc or Ill Ls/17
